{{Short description|Typographical symbol resembling a "T"}}
The '''tee''' ('''⊤''', <code>\top</code> in [[LaTeX]]), also called '''down tack''' (as opposed to the [[up tack]]) or '''verum''',<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Polkowski |first=Lech T. |date=2023 |title=Logic: Reference Book for Computer Scientists |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-42034-4 |journal=Intelligent Systems Reference Library |volume=245 |pages=180 |doi=10.1007/978-3-031-42034-4 |isbn=978-3-031-42033-7 |issn=1868-4394|url-access=subscription }}</ref> is a [[symbol]] used to represent:
* The [[truth value]] of being true in [[logic]], or a sentence (e.g., [[formula]] in [[propositional calculus]]) which is unconditionally true.<ref>{{cite web |title=tautology {{!}} Definition & Facts |website=Encyclopedia Britannica |language=en |url=https://www.britannica.com/topic/tautology |access-date=2020-08-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Definition of TAUTOLOGY |language=en |website=www.merriam-webster.com |url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/tautology |access-date=2020-08-14}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |last=Weisstein |first=Eric W. |title=Tautology |language=en |website=mathworld.wolfram.com |url=https://mathworld.wolfram.com/Tautology.html |access-date=2020-08-14}}</ref> By definition, every [[Tautology (logic)|tautology]] is [[logical equivalence|logically equivalent]] to the verum.
* The [[top type]] in [[type theory]].
* The [[top element]] in [[lattice theory]].
* [[Mixed radix]] encoding in the [[APL (programming language)|APL programming language]].
* A [[Raising_(sound_change)|lowered]] [[Phonetic|phonic]] in the [[International Phonetic Alphabet]] and [[phonetics]]. In this usage, it is usually written under the primary IPA symbol.

A similar-looking superscript T may be used to mean the [[transpose]] of a matrix.

==Encoding==
In [[Unicode]], the tee character is encoded as {{Unichar|22A4|DOWN TACK|html=}}.<ref>{{cite web |title=Mathematical Operators – Unicode |url=https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U2200.pdf |accessdate=2013-07-20}}</ref> The symbol is encoded in [[LaTeX]] as <code>\top</code>.

A large variant is encoded as {{Unichar|27D9|LARGE DOWN TACK|html=}} in the Unicode block [[Miscellaneous Mathematical Symbols-A]].
